questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were a few. For one Vancouver's nature is so different from the one i Denmark and I really wanted to experience that first hand (hikes in the mountains). Secondly, I was intrigued by the fact that Canada is so culturally and ethnically multifaceted, which is interesting to experience as an anthropology student. Lastly, I have only heard great things about UBC and the level of education available for me there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Loved the city and country but was not in love with the way they test and grade you at UBC (all the multiple choice testing).

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had some introduction classes on zoom before arrival as well as an introductory day ("Imagine Day") where we got all the information we needed as well as getting to meet some of the other exchange students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: We had a good experience finding a place with AirBnb

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Kitsilano - Downtown feels less safe and the bus ride to and off campus is really long. Stay far away from east Hastings St.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not a lot of spaces . maybe it's an error on my behalf but I was convinced that here was a mandatory food plan with student housing. This is not true.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration is fairly easy. Go to the student service center website and on the page "registration" you can add and delete courses. At UBC it's normal to shop around for courses, so don't be afraid to pick something as your choice will not be final before about two weeks into the semester (they will tell you about this on Imagine Day)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Zoom classes and Imagine Day

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try some classes out before making your final choice

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Loved the classes, the instructors, and the curriculum. However I did not enjoy the tasting based on how much you could remember from the texts. I would have loved more emphasis on applying and understanding the things learned in class.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Mostly took 200 classes

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty much the same but the testing and exams are very different

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ANTH 210 - Eating Culture
ANTH 203 - Anthropology of Drugs
ANTH 206 - Witches, Vampires, and Zombies: Anthropology of the Supernatural
SOCI 250 - Crime and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Loved them all. Really loved the instructor I had in SOCI 250 (Chris something) and I really learned valuable stuff in ANTH 203 Anthropology of Drugs

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If you can't get an E-sim a phone plan is quite expensive (60 CAD) and overall the food (especially organic and just vegetables in general) is soo unbelievably expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were definitely more expensive but the cost of dining out was less expensive (sushi is really high quality and very cheap compared to danish prices)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different clubs that you can join for a small fee (fx an outdoor club or surfclub)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely go on the surftrip to Tofino, and otherwise just take advantage of being around mountains and go on a lot of hikes. Would recommend panorama ridge and going to Washington to hike in North Cascades National Park. Use the summer (when it starts to rain and snow hiking will become much harder and less enjoyable)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Vancouver Island (Victoria city centre is much cuter than downtown Vancouver), North Cascades, Panorama Ridge, Whistler, if you like electronic music download the app Resident Advisor, which will show you events, go to concerts (there is a lot more artists passing through Vancouver than Denmark)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I think it's the easiest to get to know canadian students if you participate in some of the clubs and take some seminar classes, which will be more based on group work and have a much smaller class compared to lectures

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The school system

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness of Canadians - they are much less reserved, if they like something you wear they compliment it, they say thank you every time they get off the bus, and always stop for pedestrians crossing the roas even though there are no crosswalk

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Live off campus in Kitsilano if you want to experience more of Vancouver, live on campus if you want to socialize, eat sushi and go on hikes (if you can go to Vancouver as early possible to get the most out of the summer)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing Canadian culture and nature

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The school structure

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
